mainTopic: Valid shoes and feet for חליצה: who wrote the ברייתא, אמימר's rulings, how far the רגל reaches, and the story of סיסרא and יעל
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא listing when חליצה is valid and when it is not. The גמרא asks who wrote it, since it accepts a wooden leg but rejects a cloth shoe. אביי says it all follows the רבנן, and the wooden leg was covered in leather. רבא rejects this and says it all follows רבי מאיר: the shoe need not be leather, but it must protect the foot. אמימר then rules that the יבם must press his foot down, and that a man who walks on the backs of his feet cannot do חליצה. Both rulings survive challenges from רב אשי. Next the גמרא explains, from the words ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״, why a man whose leg is cut off below the knee can still do חליצה but one cut off above the knee cannot. It answers several פסוקים that seem to call the thighs רגלים by saying they are polite ways of speaking. Finally, רבי יוחנן teaches about סיסרא and יעל, and the גמרא asks how יעל could take pleasure from a sin. The answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: More cases where חליצה is valid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of valid cases. Whether the יבם stands, sits or leans, and even if he is blind, the חליצה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether he is standing, sitting, or leaning, and a woman who does חליצה with a blind man: her חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the middle of a ברייתא. It is finishing its list of situations where חליצה is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The position of the יבם's body does not matter for חליצה. Being blind does not disqualify him either. These items continue a list that began earlier with the wooden leg (קב הקיטע).

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony of removing the יבם's shoe, which frees the widow from יבום

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עוֹמֵד, בֵּין יוֹשֵׁב, בֵּין מוּטֶּה,
phrases.english: Whether he is standing, whether sitting, whether leaning,
phrases.notes: "He" is the יבם, the brother-in-law whose shoe she takes off.

phrases.english: and a woman who does חליצה with a blind man

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין עוֹמֵד, בֵּין יוֹשֵׁב, בֵּין מוּטֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began just before this section with the case of קב הקיטע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Body position does not affect חליצה, and חליצה with a blind יבם is valid.

steps.title: Cases where חליצה is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now lists cases where the חליצה does not work. These include a torn shoe, a broken sandal, hand blocks, a cloth shoe, and a יבם who is a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with a torn shoe that does not cover most of the foot, a broken sandal that does not hold most of the foot, hand blocks, a cloth shoe, or with a minor: her חליצה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא switches to cases where חליצה is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shoe must cover or hold most of the foot, or it does not count as a shoe. Hand blocks are not worn on the foot. A cloth shoe is invalid, which hints that the shoe has to be made of leather, and this is the detail the גמרא will pick up on. A יבם who is a קטן also cannot do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A shoe that is torn open
A sandal that is broken or damaged
Hand blocks an amputee uses to push himself along

phrases.english: that does not cover most of the foot,
that does not hold most of the foot,

phrases.notes: These are like leather pads an amputee wears on his hands so he can drag himself along.

phrases.english: and with a soft shoe made of cloth,
and a woman who does חליצה with a minor

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּמִנְעָל הַנִּפְרָם שֶׁאֵין חוֹפֶה אֶת רוֹב הָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the valid cases with invalid ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A damaged shoe, hand blocks, a cloth shoe, or a minor יבם make the חליצה invalid.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling on the cloth shoe sets up the גמרא's question about which תנא wrote this ברייתא.

steps.title: Who holds that a wooden leg counts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא would accept an amputee's wooden leg for חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The amputee's wooden leg: whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case of the ברייתא and asks which תנא it follows. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting a wooden leg as a 'shoe' is a surprising position. The גמרא wants to find a תנא who holds this view elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: The wooden leg of an amputee

phrases.english: The amputee's wooden leg: whose opinion is this?
phrases.notes: This refers to the start of the ברייתא, just before our section, which allowed חליצה with a wooden leg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from quoting the ברייתא to analyzing who wrote it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a wooden leg counts as a shoe?

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר, based on the laws of שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is רבי מאיר. A משנה in שבת says he allows an amputee to go out on שבת with his wooden leg, while רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, as we learned: an amputee may go out on שבת with his wooden leg; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. It proves this from a משנה about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats a wooden leg like a shoe, so wearing it on שבת is not carrying. A shoe for חליצה works the same way, so he would accept it for חליצה too. רבי יוסי does not see it as a shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Goes out (on שבת, into a public area)

phrases.english: as we learned: an amputee may go out with his wooden leg,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שבת. "Going out" means walking into a public area on שבת.

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who treats a wooden leg as a shoe for שבת.

steps.title: But the cloth shoe sounds like the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the same ברייתא rejects a cloth shoe, and that sounds like the רבנן, who require a real shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a cloth shoe, it is invalid. So now we have come to the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The end of the ברייתא seems to follow a different opinion than its beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר does not care what the shoe is made of, he should allow a cloth shoe. Rejecting cloth fits the רבנן, who side with רבי יוסי. So the ברייתא seems to switch opinions partway through.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (the opinion of)
The Sages, the majority view (here agreeing with רבי יוסי)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about cloth shoes themselves. The problem is that one ברייתא seems to follow two different תנאים.

phrases.english: With a soft shoe made of cloth, it is invalid,
so we have come to the רבנן!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 4's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling against a cloth shoe matches the רבנן, so the first part (רבי מאיר) and the last part (רבנן) would follow two different opinions.

steps.title: אביי: the whole ברייתא is the רבנן, and the wooden leg was covered in leather
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that because the end of the ברייתא follows the רבנן, the beginning does too. The wooden leg in the first case was covered with leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: since the last part is the רבנן, the first part is also the רבנן. The first part is talking about a wooden leg covered with leather.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by saying the whole ברייתא follows the רבנן. He reads the first case in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of splitting the ברייתא between two תנאים, אביי keeps one author, the רבנן. Even the רבנן accept a wooden leg if it is covered in leather, because then it works like a leather shoe. This answer drops the earlier claim that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the whole ברייתא follows the רבנן. A shoe for חליצה must be leather, and a wooden leg works only if it is covered in leather.

phrases.english: Since the last part is the רבנן,
the first part is also the רבנן.
And the first part is talking about one covered with leather.
phrases.notes: He means the wooden leg from the start of the ברייתא was covered in leather.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבָּנַן, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by putting the whole ברייתא under the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the first case is limited to a leather-covered wooden leg
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר and accepts any wooden leg.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן throughout, and the wooden leg was covered with leather.

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי's leather-covering answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if אביי were right, the ברייתא should have drawn the line inside the wooden-leg case itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: According to you, a wooden leg not covered with leather would be unfit. If so, the ברייתא should not have taught a separate case of a cloth shoe at the end. It should have split the wooden-leg case itself: this is only when it is covered with leather, but without leather it is unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer from step 6. He says the ברייתא's wording does not fit that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אביי is right, a wooden leg without leather would be unfit. That would be the most natural place for the ברייתא to show the difference between leather and non-leather. Since the ברייתא used a separate example (a cloth shoe) instead, רבא concludes that אביי's reading is unlikely.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you say is true)
Let it make the distinction within that same case
When is this said? (a phrase that limits a ruling)

phrases.english: But if it is not covered with leather,
instead of teaching in the end part a cloth shoe,
let it make the distinction in this case itself:
When it is covered with leather,
but if it is not covered with leather, it is unfit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אֲבָל אֵין מְחוּפֶּה עוֹר, מַאי — פָּסוּל? אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the wooden leg in the ברייתא was covered with leather
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If leather covering were what mattered, the ברייתא would have drawn the line inside the wooden-leg case. It would not have brought a separate cloth-shoe case.

steps.title: רבא: the whole ברייתא follows רבי מאיר; protection is the key
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the entire ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. A wooden leg protects the foot, while a cloth shoe does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Since the beginning follows רבי מאיר, the end also follows רבי מאיר. This one (the wooden leg) protects the foot, and that one (the cloth shoe) does not protect it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own way to solve the contradiction from step 5. He reads the whole ברייתא as following רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read the beginning to match the end, which follows the רבנן. רבא does the opposite and reads the end to match the beginning, which follows רבי מאיר. According to רבי מאיר, a shoe does not have to be leather, but it must protect the foot. A wooden leg does that, while a soft cloth shoe does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a teaching

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says the whole ברייתא follows the רבנן, and the wooden leg was covered with leather. רבא says it all follows רבי מאיר: the material does not matter, but the shoe must protect the foot.

phrases.english: Since the beginning follows Rabbi Meir,
the end also follows Rabbi Meir:

phrases.notes: "This one" is the wooden leg, which is hard enough to protect the foot.

phrases.english: and that one does not protect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: מִדְּרֵישָׁא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, סֵיפָא נָמֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new answer to the קשיא from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the whole ברייתא to one תנא (רבי מאיר) and explains the difference between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cloth-shoe case seemed to show that the ברייתא requires leather, like the רבנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי מאיר rules out a cloth shoe, because it does not protect the foot. The wooden leg does protect it.

steps.title: אמימר: the יבם must press his foot down
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that the יבם must press his foot down when the חליצה is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: One who has חליצה done must press his foot down.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts here. אמימר adds a rule about how the יבם holds his foot during חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya was about which shoes are valid. Now it moves to the יבם's position. אמימר requires him to press his foot down, and the shoe is removed while he does so.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the shoe question to a new rule about the יבם's foot
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יבם must press his foot down during חליצה.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא allows sitting or leaning
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר from a ברייתא that allows חליצה whether the יבם stands, sits, or leans.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But it was taught: whether he is standing, sitting, or leaning!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי objects to אמימר's rule using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא accepts חליצה in any position, even leaning. Someone leaning cannot easily press his foot down. So the ברייתא seems to show that pressing the foot down is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עוֹמֵד, בֵּין יוֹשֵׁב, בֵּין מוּטֶּה!
phrases.english: whether he is standing, whether sitting, whether leaning!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's rule from step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's requirement to press the foot down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows any position, including leaning, where pressing the foot down is hard. So it seems no pressing is required.

steps.title: Any position works, as long as he presses his foot down
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא allows any position, but in every case he still presses his foot down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: really, in each case he presses his foot down.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי's challenge. He explains that the ברייתא and his rule fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only teaches that the יבם's body position does not matter. It never says the foot can be loose. Even when sitting or leaning, he must press his foot down.
steps.whatToRemember: The יבם can stand, sit, or lean during חליצה, but in every position he presses his foot down (אמימר).

phrases.english: and really, it is where he presses his foot down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the ברייתא as adding a condition it does not state
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Allowing leaning seemed to mean the foot does not need to be pressed down
steps.terutzMaskana: Any body position is fine, but the foot must always be pressed down

steps.title: A man who walks on the backs of his feet cannot do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that someone whose feet are twisted, so that he walks on their backs, cannot do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר also said: A man who walks on the backs of his feet cannot do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling from אמימר. A man whose feet are so twisted that he walks on their backs cannot do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אמימר ruled about how the יבם must stand during חליצה. Now he adds a ruling about a foot that is badly misshapen. The גמרא gives no reason here, but the answer in step 14 shows the idea: for such a man, what he wears works as his foot rather than as a shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: the back (top side) of the foot

phrases.english: on the backs of his feet,
phrases.notes: His foot is twisted over, so he steps on the top side instead of the sole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from אמימר about the יבם's foot, following his ruling about pressing the foot down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who walks on the backs of his twisted feet is not able to do חליצה.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges from a ברייתא about leg supports
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי cites a ברייתא that allows חליצה with leg supports, which seems to show that a man with twisted feet can do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But a ברייתא teaches that leg supports are valid for חליצה. Doesn't that mean the disabled man himself does חליצה with them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's ruling. A ברייתא says leg supports can be used for חליצה, and supports like these are worn by people who cannot walk on their feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leg supports are used by someone who cannot walk normally. If the ברייתא allows חליצה with them, it seems to mean that such a disabled man can do חליצה. That would go against אמימר's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: leg supports [are valid for ḥalitza]?
phrases.notes: These are supports that someone who can't walk on his feet leans on as he moves.

phrases.english: Does it not mean that he himself performs ḥalitza with them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אמימר's ruling from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's rule that a man with twisted feet cannot do חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leg supports belong to a disabled man. If חליצה with them is valid, then a disabled man can do חליצה.

steps.title: The supports were given to a different, normal man
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a man with normal feet who wore the supports. It does not mean the disabled man himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means he gave the supports to someone else, and that other man did חליצה with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי's challenge. The ברייתא means that a man with normal feet put on the supports and did חליצה with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a normal man, the supports work like a shoe, so they can be pulled off in חליצה. For the twisted-foot man, the supports act as his foot, not as a shoe. So the ברייתא does not go against אמימר.

phrases.english: No, it means he gave it to another, and that one performs ḥalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means the disabled man himself does חליצה with his supports.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a man with normal feet wore the supports, so אמימר's rule still stands.

steps.title: By אמימר's rule, בר אובא and בר קיפוף cannot do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out what follows from אמימר's ruling: two well-known men whose feet were twisted could not do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: According to what אמימר said, בר אובא cannot do חליצה, and בר קיפוף cannot do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי spells out what אמימר's ruling means in real life. Two men known in his time, בר אובא and בר קיפוף, would not be able to do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is added here. רב אשי applies the rule from step 12 to real people whose feet were twisted. It shows how far the rule reaches in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A man of רב אשי's time
Another man of רב אשי's time

phrases.english: and Bar Kipof cannot perform ḥalitza.
phrases.notes: These were two men of his time whose feet were badly twisted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְמַאי דְּקָאָמַר אַמֵּימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אמימר's rule survives the challenge, רב אשי applies it to real people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By אמימר's rule, men with twisted feet such as בר אובא and בר קיפוף cannot do חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: אמימר: a man who walks on the backs of his feet cannot do חליצה. Leg supports are valid only when a man with normal feet wears them.

steps.title: Contradiction: a prosthetic leg is not counted as a foot for the רגלים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows חליצה for a man missing his leg from the knee down, but a ברייתא says people with prosthetic legs are excluded from the מצוה of the רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: from the knee down, the חליצה is valid. But a ברייתא teaches: רגלים (feet) excludes people with prosthetic legs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and raises a contradiction. The משנה allows חליצה for a man whose leg is cut off below the knee, but a ברייתא says that people with prosthetic legs do not count as having feet for the מצוה of עליה לרגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רגלים hints that you go up to ירושלים on your own feet, and the ברייתא learns from this that someone with a prosthetic leg is left out. That suggests the Torah does not treat a prosthetic as a foot. So how can the משנה accept חליצה from someone who has no real foot?
steps.confusionAlert: Here רגלים means the three festivals, not a person's feet. The ברייתא uses the double meaning to learn that you must be able to walk up to ירושלים on your own feet.

phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: if his leg was cut off below the knee, the חליצה is valid.
שמות 23:14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's ruling about an amputated leg and sets it against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that חליצה is valid when the leg is cut off from the knee down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that a prosthetic leg does not count as a foot, so a man without a real foot should not be able to do חליצה.

steps.title: חליצה is different: the פסוק says ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״
steps.stepSummary: The חליצה פסוק says ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״, from on his foot, which includes the part of the leg above the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because it is written: ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״, from on his foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The חליצה פסוק has its own special wording, ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״ can mean the area above the foot. So for חליצה, the shoe can sit on the lower leg too, and a real foot is not needed. The רגלים still require an actual foot, so the two sources do not clash.

phrases.english: as it is written: "from on his foot."
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different פסוק wording for each מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A prosthetic does not count as a foot anywhere, so חליצה should not work either.
steps.terutzMaskana: For חליצה the פסוק includes the area above the foot, so a real foot is not required.

steps.title: If so, above the knee should work too
steps.stepSummary: If the part above the foot counts, the גמרא asks why a man missing his leg from above the knee can't do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should work above the knee too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If ״מֵעַל״ includes the area above the foot, why does the משנה stop at the knee?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows חליצה only when the leg is cut off below the knee. If "above the foot" is enough, then the thigh above the knee is also above the foot. That would make a man cut off above the knee valid too.

phrases.english: above the knee too [should be valid]!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לְמַעְלָה מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 by pushing its logic further.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״ as including the area above the foot
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everything above the foot, including the area above the knee, should count, but the משנה limits it to below the knee.

steps.title: Only one ״מֵעַל״, not ״מֵעַל״ on top of ״מֵעַל״
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק includes the area right above the foot, up to the knee, but not the area above that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says ״מֵעַל״, from on, and not "from on that which is on."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reading the word ״מֵעַל״ closely. It includes one level above the foot, not a further level beyond that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״מֵעַל״ adds the section just above the foot, the lower leg up to the knee. Going above the knee would be like being "above what is above," and the פסוק does not say that. So the משנה's limit at the knee comes straight from the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: For חליצה, ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״ includes the lower leg up to the knee, so a man missing his leg below the knee can do חליצה. Above the knee does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the source for the משנה's line at the knee, and why חליצה is treated differently from the רגלים.

phrases.english: and not "from on that which is on."
phrases.notes: The lower leg sits right above the foot. The thigh is a further step up, above the lower leg.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 and wraps up the discussion of the amputated leg.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״מֵעַל״ includes anything anywhere above the foot.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״מֵעַל״ includes only one level above the foot, up to the knee.

steps.title: רב פפא learns that the heel bone reaches the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the heel bone must reach all the way down to the ground. Otherwise the calf would be two levels above the foot and could not be used for חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that the heel bone goes all the way down to the ground. If you thought it was a separate piece, the bone itself would be 'on the foot,' and the calf would be 'on top of what is on the foot.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the rule from the last step, that the area right above the foot counts. He uses it to learn a fact about how the foot is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ״מֵעַל רַגְלוֹ״ only covers what sits directly on the foot. Since the משנה allows חליצה on the calf, the calf must sit directly on the foot. So the heel bone must be part of the foot itself, reaching down to the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: On top of what is on top, one level too far

phrases.english: that this heel bone reaches down to the ground.
For if it would enter your mind
then it would be the 'on top of' the foot,
and the calf would be 'on top of what is on top'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side conclusion from the תירוץ in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heel bone is part of the foot and reaches the ground, so the calf counts as directly 'on the foot.'

steps.title: רב אשי says the proof does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even if the heel bone is separate, anything attached to the foot counts as the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say the bone is separate, anything joined to the foot is treated like the foot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רב פפא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumed a separate bone would count as its own level. רב אשי says a bone attached to the foot is part of the foot for this purpose. So the calf is still directly 'on the foot,' and we cannot learn anything about the heel bone.

phrases.english: Even if you say it is completely separate,
anything that is attached to the foot

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof about the heel bone. It does not reject the rule about the calf.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A bone attached to the foot does not count as an extra level, so the calf counts either way.

steps.title: A פסוק calls the thighs רגלים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies the thigh is not part of the רגל. רב כהנא brings a פסוק about birth 'from between her רגלים,' which sounds like the thighs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a man missing his leg from the knee up cannot do חליצה. רב כהנא objected from the פסוק: 'And her afterbirth that comes out from between her legs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words about 'from the knee and above.' רב כהנא challenges the idea that רגל stops at the knee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the thigh as outside the רגל. But a baby comes out from between the thighs, and the פסוק calls that 'between her רגלים.' So it seems רגל can include the thigh.

phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה: a man missing his leg from the knee up cannot do חליצה.

phrases.english: "And her afterbirth that comes out from between her legs"!
phrases.notes: דברים 28:57

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in step 19 and in the משנה: רגל stops at the knee.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the thigh is not part of the רגל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses רגלים for the area where birth happens, which is between the thighs.

steps.title: אביי: during birth her heels touch her thighs
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a woman crouching to give birth presses her heels against her thighs, so the baby really comes out between her feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When she crouches to give birth, she presses her heels into her thighs and gives birth.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב כהנא by explaining what 'between her feet' looks like during birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a crouching position the feet are pulled up right next to the body. So the birth really is 'between her feet,' and רגליה can keep its simple meaning of feet.

phrases.english: When she crouches to give birth,
she presses her heels into her thighs

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the real-life situation the פסוק describes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Between her רגלים' means between her thighs.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Between her רגלים' really means between her feet, because her feet are pressed against her body.

steps.title: 'He had not done his רגלים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק about not grooming 'his רגלים,' which refers to a body area higher than the feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'He had not dressed his feet, nor trimmed his mustache'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק where רגליו seems to mean a part of the body above the knee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grooming 'his רגלים' here does not mean the feet. It refers to a higher, private area of the body. That seems to show that רגל can reach above the knee.

phrases.notes: שמואל ב 19:25. The גמרא understands 'his feet' here as a private area higher up, not the actual feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge of the same kind as step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that רגל does not go above the knee.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here רגליו refers to a body area above the knee.

steps.title: A polite way of speaking
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק uses רגליו as a polite way to refer to a private area. It does not tell us what רגל really means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a clean way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is speaking politely and is not defining the word רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנ״ך sometimes avoids blunt words for private matters. When it does, the word used is a stand-in. It does not prove anything about how far the word normally reaches.
steps.whatToRemember: When a פסוק uses a polite stand-in word, you cannot use it to define that word for halacha.

phrases.english: It is a refined way of speaking.
phrases.notes: The פסוק uses 'feet' to avoid saying something blunt, so it tells us nothing about where the רגל ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Euphemism: the word is not meant literally
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רגליו here really means the upper body area.
steps.terutzMaskana: רגליו is a polite stand-in word, not a definition.

steps.title: שאול went 'to cover his רגלים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק where שאול goes into a cave 'to cover his רגלים,' meaning to relieve himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And שאול went in to cover his feet'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק where רגליו seems to mean a part of the body above the knee.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering 'his רגלים' here describes going to the bathroom. That act involves the area above the thighs, so it seems רגל goes higher than the knee.

phrases.notes: שמואל א 24:3
This means he went in to relieve himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וַיָּבֹא שָׁאוּל לְהָסֵךְ אֶת רַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge of the same kind.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that רגל does not go above the knee.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here רגליו refers to the area involved in relieving oneself, which is above the knee.

steps.title: Again, a polite way of speaking
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: 'covering his רגלים' is a polite way to say he relieved himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a clean way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: the פסוק is just speaking politely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק avoids describing the bathroom directly, so it uses רגליו instead. This tells us nothing about where the רגל ends for חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: His feet, used here as a polite stand-in word

phrases.english: It is a refined way of speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 the same way step 25 answered step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רגליו here really means the upper body area.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a polite stand-in word.

steps.title: עגלון 'covering his רגלים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק about עגלון, king of מואב, whose servants thought he was 'covering his רגלים' in his private room.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Surely he is covering his feet in the cool room'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק that uses the same phrase about covering the feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the פסוק about שאול, this one describes relieving oneself as 'covering his רגלים.' Again it seems רגל can refer to the area above the knee.

keyTerms.meaning: The cool room, a private chamber

phrases.notes: שופטים 3:24

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַךְ מֵסִיךְ הוּא רַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge of the same kind.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that רגל does not go above the knee.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Covering his רגלים' refers to the area above the knee.

steps.title: Polite language again
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: the פסוק is speaking politely.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a clean way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same reply: this is polite language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the תנ״ך uses 'covering the feet' as a polite phrase, this פסוק adds nothing new. It cannot define the word רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The king of מואב in this פסוק

phrases.english: It is a refined way of speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רגליו here really means the upper body area.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a polite stand-in word.

steps.title: סיסרא fell 'between her רגלים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק about סיסרא and יעל, 'between her רגלים,' which hints at relations between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between her feet,' and so on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one last פסוק where רגליה seems to mean the thighs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק hints that סיסרא and יעל had relations. That would involve the thighs, not the feet, so it seems רגל can include the thigh.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on: the פסוק continues
The enemy general killed by יעל

phrases.notes: שופטים 5:27. The 'etc.' means the rest of the פסוק continues: he sank, he fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge of the same kind.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that רגל does not go above the knee.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Between her רגלים' refers to relations, which involve the thighs.

steps.title: This too is polite language
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: the פסוק speaks politely, so the rule stands that רגל stops at the knee.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a clean way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge the same way. This closes the series of challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פסוק brought here uses רגל as a polite stand-in word for something private. None of them defines the word. So the משנה's rule holds: for חליצה, the רגל goes up to the knee and no higher.
steps.whatToRemember: For חליצה, the רגל includes the foot and the leg up to the knee, but not the thigh. פסוקים that seem to use רגל for higher body parts are just speaking politely.

phrases.english: It is a refined way of speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30 and finishes the set of challenges.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Between her רגלים' means between her thighs.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a polite stand-in phrase, so the knee remains the limit of the רגל.

steps.title: סיסרא was with יעל seven times that day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the פסוק in שירת דבורה that סיסרא was with יעל seven times on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: That wicked man, סיסרא, was with יעל seven times on that day. We learn this from the פסוק: 'Between her feet he knelt, he fell, he lay; between her feet he knelt, he fell; where he knelt, there he fell, destroyed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new statement from רבי יוחנן that tells us more about what happened between סיסרא and יעל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step the גמרא said 'between her רגלים' hints at relations. Now רבי יוחנן goes further. He counts the action words in the פסוק (knelt, fell, lay), and there are seven of them, so each one stands for a separate time.

phrases.english: that wicked man on that day,
phrases.notes: "That wicked man" is סיסרא, from the פסוק we just saw.

phrases.english: "Between her feet he knelt, he fell, he lay;
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:27. Count the action words in the whole פסוק: there are seven, one for each time.

phrases.english: between her feet he knelt, he fell;
where he knelt, there he fell, destroyed."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁבַע בְּעִילוֹת בָּעַל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק of סיסרא and יעל from step 30 and adds a new aggadic teaching about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the seven action words in שופטים 5:27 we learn that סיסרא was with יעל seven times that day.

steps.title: But יעל got pleasure from a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how יעל could do this, since she got pleasure from a forbidden act.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she was getting pleasure from a sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's teaching. If יעל was with סיסרא, she benefited from a sin, so how could this be acceptable?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if יעל had a good goal of weakening סיסרא so she could kill him, the act was still forbidden. The problem is the pleasure she got from it. That pleasure looks like enjoying an עבירה.

phrases.english: But she was getting pleasure from a sin!
phrases.notes: "She" is יעל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story told in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching that יעל was with סיסרא seven times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having relations with סיסרא gave יעל pleasure from a forbidden act, and that should not be allowed even for a good purpose.

steps.title: The start of the answer: the 'good' that רשעים give
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, begins to answer with a rule about any good thing that comes from רשעים. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: All the good of the wicked...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to the question about יעל's pleasure. The sentence is not finished here, so this step sets up the rest of the answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that something happened. Instead it starts a general rule about any benefit or 'good' that comes from רשעים like סיסרא. This rule will explain why יעל is not seen as truly benefiting from the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא whose teaching רבי יוחנן is quoting

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. Don't try to figure out the answer from these words alone. The rest of the rule comes on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
All the good of the wicked —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: כׇּל טוֹבָתָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle about benefit that comes from רשעים (continued on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעל enjoyed a forbidden act, so what she did was wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rule about the 'good' that comes from רשעים will show that יעל's pleasure does not count as a real benefit from sin. The rule is finished on the next amud.
